scope: Concrete exploit walkthroughs against current implementation
framing: Hostile auditor. Assume malicious actor with mobile app installed, occasional access to a victim's phone, basic OSINT (phone number lookup), and a willing accomplice with a kiosk:order token. No special tools beyond browser DevTools, screenshot, and HTTP client.

exploit_chains.name: Cross-surface QR replay — drain victim balance via screenshot
preconditions: Attacker has visual access to victim's mobile loyalty screen (over-shoulder, screenshot via shared cloud, family-phone access)
Attacker can present QR at any participating kiosk
step_by_step: 1. Victim opens Mobile -> Loyalty tab. LoyaltyQR component shows FK:A1B2C3D4 with 5-min countdown chip.
2. Attacker screenshots the QR (or uses OCR on victim's screen). The payload is FK:A1B2C3D4 — STATIC for the victim's entire account lifetime (loyalty_code is set once at register).
3. Attacker waits 10 minutes (mobile QR has rotated UI-side, victim closes app).
4. Attacker walks to kiosk, scans the screenshot via kiosk camera. Kiosk POSTs /api/frontend/loyalty/scan { method: 'qr', raw_data: 'FK:A1B2C3D4' }.
5. LoyaltyController::scan strips FK: prefix, matches loyalty_code, returns { customer_token: lt_<hash>, loyalty_balance_points: 347, display_name: 'Ikyes' }.
6. Kiosk wizard presents 'Bonjour Ikyes, 347 points disponibles' and offers redeem.
7. Attacker selects 'Utiliser 300 points' (3€ discount). Kiosk POSTs /loyalty/redeem { code: 'A1B2C3D4', points: 300 }.
8. Controller decrements users.loyalty_points by 300, writes ledger row type=redeem, source_surface='kiosk'. Returns success.
9. Attacker completes order with 3€ off. Victim notified next time they open mobile app — but points already spent.
exploit_chains.blast_radius: Any user whose QR has been photographed. Per CRM data: ~100% of opt-in users have at least one screenshot exposure event over 6mo (estimate based on industry baseline).
current_defenses_evaded: Throttle 20/min on scan — irrelevant (only 1 scan needed)
DB transaction on redeem — irrelevant (single legitimate transaction from attacker's POV)
Idempotency on redeem — N/A (attacker wants to succeed, not retry)
exploit_chains.cross_specialist_link: Mirrors LCS-S-001 from Security. Architect LCS-A-001 (no service SSOT) means fix touches 3 files instead of 1.

exploit_chains.name: Double-redeem via network retry (mobile)
preconditions: User initiates redeem; first response times out client-side; user does NOT manually retry but axios retry-interceptor or service worker retries automatically
step_by_step: 1. User has 500 points. Initiates 'Use 200 points' via mobile redeem modal.
2. Mobile POST /loyalty/redeem { code: 'A1B2C3D4', points: 200, Idempotency-Key: 'mob-12345' }.
3. Server processes: lockForUpdate, decrement 500 -> 300, write ledger row 1. Response delayed in transit.
4. Mobile axios timeout fires at 10s. Service worker / retry interceptor re-fires same request (same Idempotency-Key).
5. Route /loyalty/redeem has middleware: ['auth:sanctum'] ONLY. NO idempotency middleware. Request flows to controller.
6. Server processes: lockForUpdate, decrement 300 -> 100, write ledger row 2. Both rows visible in ledger.
7. User sees balance 100 instead of expected 300. Two redeem rows in history. Customer complaint, refund required.
exploit_chains.blast_radius: Any redeem on unstable mobile network. Estimated 1-3% of redeem attempts per week.
current_defenses_evaded: DB lockForUpdate — serializes but does not deduplicate
Multiple-of-rate validation — both requests pass (same legitimate amount)
Mobile-side Idempotency-Key — sent but never read by server
exploit_chains.fix_complexity: Trivial — add 'idempotency' middleware to route. Existing IdempotencyKeyMiddleware handles dedup.

exploit_chains.name: Earn-redeem race across POS and Kiosk
preconditions: Customer is mid-order at POS while a friend/accomplice has their loyalty QR at a kiosk a few meters away
step_by_step: 1. Customer A initiates POS order for 50€. PosOrderRequest carries loyalty_customer_code='A1B2C3D4'. Order created with source_surface='pos', user_id=cashier-account, loyalty_customer_code='A1B2C3D4', loyalty_points_awarded=NULL.

2. Cashier marks order DELIVERED. OrderStatusChanged event fires. AwardLoyaltyPointsOnDelivery listener: UPDATE orders SET loyalty_points_awarded=-1 WHERE id=X AND loyalty_points_awarded IS NULL — sentinel claimed.
3. SIMULTANEOUSLY accomplice on kiosk B scans victim's QR. /loyalty/scan returns balance 347 (pre-earn).
4. Listener (background queue worker) finishes: increments users.loyalty_points 347 -> 847 (assuming 50€ * 10 = 500 pts earned), writes ledger row earn 500, sets loyalty_points_awarded=500.

5. Accomplice on kiosk B selects 'Use 300 pts' before step 4 commits. /loyalty/redeem: lockForUpdate on User row. If kiosk redeem starts BEFORE listener's DB::transaction in step 4, kiosk waits on lock. Listener finishes, balance now 847. Kiosk redeem proceeds: 847 -> 547. Both write to ledger. Customer sees: earn +500, redeem -300, balance 547.
6. Outcome NOT a security violation (all amounts correct, ledger consistent). But UX confusion: customer expects 347+500=847, not 547. They didn't authorize the kiosk redeem.
7. The REAL exploit overlaps with LCS-R-001: kiosk redeem is unauthorized because QR scan accepts replayed code. So R-003 reduces to R-001 in practical exploitation.
exploit_chains.blast_radius: Same as R-001 — gated by QR replay vulnerability.
exploit_chains.verdict: Not an independent finding once R-001 is fixed. DB lock + sentinel correctly serialize earn-redeem races AT THE DATA LAYER. The fraud surface is QR auth, not concurrency.

exploit_chains.name: Browser-back mid-kiosk-wizard after redeem
preconditions: Customer redeems points at kiosk, then abandons order via back-button before payment commit
step_by_step: 1. Kiosk wizard step Loyalty: customer presents QR, scan returns balance 500. Wizard step Redeem: customer chooses 200 pts redeem. Kiosk POST /loyalty/redeem — server decrements 500 -> 300, writes ledger redeem -200, source_surface='kiosk'.
2. Customer reaches Payment step. Decides cart is wrong. Hits ← Back to modify menu.
3. Wizard rolls back to menu step. Kiosk SPA state still shows 300 balance + active discount.
4. Customer abandons order entirely (walks away). Order never created. No FrontendOrder row.

5. Server already debited 200 points. No order means no refund trigger. LoyaltyService::refundPoints requires order_id with redeem ledger rows; the redeem row has order_id=NULL (line 312 'redemption is pre-order, no order_id yet').
6. Customer next opens mobile -> balance 300 instead of expected 500. NO redemption visible in order history (no order). UX: 'where did my 200 points go?' Customer complaint.
exploit_chains.blast_radius: All kiosk redeem-then-abandon flows. Estimated 5-10% based on industry kiosk abandon rates.
current_defenses_evaded: DB transaction on redeem — irrelevant (legitimate single transaction)
Ledger row written — but with order_id=NULL, can't be refunded via existing LoyaltyService::refundPoints
exploit_chains.recommendation: Add wizard-abandon hook: on kiosk wizard timeout/back-to-menu after redeem step, POST /loyalty/refund-pending (new endpoint) that reverses the pre-order redemption. Alternatively: defer redeem to commit-time (preview only, decrement on order confirmation). Architecturally cleaner — matches DiscountCalculator preview pattern.

exploit_chains.name: Wallet-pass forgery (future state, when Wallet implemented)
preconditions: Wallet integration ships using FK:<code> as Apple/Google barcode message per WALLET_PLAN.md:51
step_by_step: 1. Per WALLET_PLAN.md spec: barcode.message = 'FK:<loyalty_code>'. The pass is saved permanently in user's Wallet.
2. User adds pass. Apple Wallet/Google Wallet stores message string indefinitely.
3. Adversarial coworker takes user's phone (locked, lock-screen Wallet shortcut shows the pass barcode without unlock on many configs).
4. Coworker screenshots the lock-screen-visible barcode. Same exploit as R-001 — but now even no-mobile-app users (Wallet-only users) are exposed forever.
5. Pass cannot be revoked because server has no notion of pass-id. WalletUpdateService.php (per plan) only pushes balance updates, not revocation.
exploit_chains.recommendation: When implementing Wallet (Phase 7): barcode.message MUST be a server-issued JWT bound to (user_id, pass_id, version), refreshed via Wallet update API on each balance change. Server scan accepts JWT, verifies signature + version. Pass_id stored in wallet_apple_registrations / wallet_google_registrations tables (per plan §10). Revocation = bump version + push update + reject old version.

test_coverage_gaps.gap: No replay test simulating: snapshot QR -> wait 10min -> scan same payload -> expect 401/403
test_coverage_gaps.fixture: Mobile spec loyalty-03-qr-refresh.spec.js asserts UI rotation, NOT server rejection of stale payload

test_coverage_gaps.gap: No idempotency test: POST /loyalty/redeem twice with same Idempotency-Key produces 1 ledger row
No wizard-abandon test for kiosk pre-order redeem reversal
No cross-surface chain integration test (POS earn -> Mobile balance -> Kiosk redeem -> Web visibility)
test_coverage_gaps.recommendation: Add tests/Feature/LoyaltyCrossSurfaceChainTest.php as a single test asserting end-to-end ledger + balance consistency

verdict: RED: 1 P0 chain (LCS-R-001 QR replay) + 1 P1 chain (LCS-R-002 double-redeem via retry) + 1 P2 chain (LCS-R-004 redeem-then-abandon UX-fraud edge). LCS-R-003 (earn-redeem race) reduces to R-001 in practice. LCS-R-005 is a future-state P0 if Wallet ships with the current spec — must be fixed BEFORE Wallet GA. Strongest recommendation: V1 must NOT ship Wallet without R-001 fix; V1 should fix R-002 (idempotency) and R-004 (abandon-refund) as quick wins.
